summary: End-to-end testing of the Bulk Property Manager feature (backend + frontend). Wrote 14 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_bulk_manager.py — ALL PASS (14/14). Covers bulk-edit whitelist, non-whitelisted key filtering (owner_id/status/images silently dropped, only monthly_price applied), title_prefix idempotence, amenities append (no-dup merge) vs replace, ownership forbidden skipping for non-owners, admin override, snapshot round-trip undo, and 400 for empty payloads. Bulk-images: shared fan-out appends to images[], per_property mode assigns distinct urls, ownership check enforced, 400 on empty ids. Verified no MongoDB _id leaks in responses. Frontend Playwright: tab-bulk-manager visible for owner / hidden for renter; 33 rows rendered for owner; search + rental filter narrow list correctly; select-all toggles count; BulkEditModal shows 'Pick at least one field to apply' toast on empty save; valid save with has_elevator apply-tick returns 'Updated 33 properties' and closes modal; Undo button appears after save and produces 'Reverted last bulk edit' toast; BulkPhotosModal opens, shared↔per-property modes switch (33 per-property drop rows), 'Add at least one photo' toast on empty save.

backend_coverage.Non-whitelisted keys silently dropped (o: PASS — only monthly_price applied, snapshot keys = ['monthly_price']

critical_code_review_comments: BulkManagerTab.jsx:97 — handleUndo loops sequentially over ALL snapshots with one bulk-edit POST per id (e.g. 33 POSTs for a 33-property undo). Works, but noisy. Consider grouping snapshots that share the same key-set into a single bulk-edit call per group.

BulkManagerTab.jsx:325 — `title_prefix: applyMap.title_prefix ? (titlePrefix||'').trim() : null`. Backend treats null as 'no prefix' via `bool((body.title_prefix or '').strip())`, so that's fine, but passing an empty string after a user ticks Apply with no value silently no-ops. Consider a small validation toast.

properties.py:303 — amenities_mode='append' only merges when `amenities` key is in patch; replace mode without amenities in patch is a no-op (correct). The snapshot captures the PRE-merge amenities list, so Undo will restore original amenities exactly — verified.

properties.py:316 — snapshot = {k: existing.get(k) for k in patch.keys()} captures the resolved `patch` keys (post-merge), so Undo snapshot contains the original amenities value even though patch['amenities'] is the merged list. Good.

BulkManagerTab.jsx is 759 lines (BulkManagerTab + BulkEditModal + BulkPhotosModal + DropZone + PhotoThumb). Exceeds the 700-line guideline — consider splitting BulkEditModal / BulkPhotosModal into their own files for maintainability.
Minor: rental_type filter in BulkManagerTab only checks exact match on `p.rental_type`; no issues, just pointing out that lower/upper-cased values would not match (data is normalized).

No client-side cap on how many properties can be edited at once; for users with hundreds of listings one bulk-edit POST is fine (server iterates) but the Undo could balloon to hundreds of calls — see first item.

No residual data left in DB. The frontend test executed one bulk-edit+undo roundtrip on all 33 of owner@test.com's existing properties; since Undo restored snapshots, end-state matches pre-test state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature fully validated end-to-end. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_bulk_manager.py. Pytest xml: /app/test_reports/pytest/bulk_manager.xml. Key invariants confirmed: (a) server snapshot accurately reflects pre-change values so Undo is safe even for amenities append; (b) _BULK_EDITABLE_FIELDS whitelist rejects owner_id/status/images silently; (c) amenities append de-dupes; (d) ownership check skips non-owned ids with reason='forbidden' for both bulk-edit and bulk-images; (e) admin bypass works. Frontend uses sessionStorage (not localStorage) for token — note for future Playwright scripts.
